title: When a language falls silent
text:
Linguists estimate that around half of the world's seven thousand languages could disappear by the end of this century. The process is rarely sudden. More often, parents [[1]] their children to use the dominant language of the region, believing it will open more doors, and within two generations the old tongue has all but [[2]] out. By the time anyone thinks to record it, only a handful of elderly speakers may remain.

Why should this matter to anyone else? Supporters of revival projects are keen to [[3]] attention to what is at stake. Every language, they argue, holds a unique body of knowledge, from the names of medicinal plants to ways of describing the landscape that have no [[4]] in any other tongue.

Revival is possible, but it is painstaking work. Projects are often heavily [[5]] on the enthusiasm of a few individuals, and progress can be slow. Some communities have [[6]] remarkable results by setting up 'language nests', where young children spend their days with fluent elders. Others have turned to technology, recording conversations and building apps so that learners can practise at their own [[7]]. [[8]] these efforts, few experts believe that every endangered language can be saved.

explanation.en: The gap is followed by object + 'to' infinitive ('their children to use'), and only 'encourage somebody to do' has this pattern. 'Suggest' and 'demand' need a 'that'-clause here, and 'insist' needs 'on' or 'that'.
explanation.cs: Za mezerou je předmět + to + infinitiv, což umí jen 'encourage sb to do' (povzbuzovat někoho k). Častá chyba Čechů je 'suggest sb to do'; správně je 'suggest that ...'.

explanation.en: 'Die out' means to disappear completely, which is what happens to the old tongue: 'has all but died out'. 'Run out' is used for supplies that are used up, not for a language falling out of use.
explanation.cs: 'Die out' = vymřít, zaniknout (o jazycích, druzích, zvycích). 'Run out' znamená dojít (např. čas, peníze), ne zaniknout.

explanation.en: The collocation is 'draw attention to': 'keen to draw attention to what is at stake'. 'Catch' combines with 'attention' only without 'to' ('catch somebody's attention').
explanation.cs: Kolokace 'draw attention to sth' = upozornit na něco. 'Catch sb's attention' (upoutat pozornost) existuje, ale bez 'to' a s osobou.

explanation.en: 'Have no equivalent in another language' means there is no word with the same meaning there. 'Resemblance' describes looking alike, and 'no resemblance in any other tongue' is not a natural phrase.
explanation.cs: 'No equivalent in' = nemá obdobu, ekvivalent v jiném jazyce. 'Resemblance' je vnější podobnost (např. mezi sourozenci), ne slovo se stejným významem.

explanation.en: The gap is followed by 'on', and only 'reliant on' takes this preposition: projects depend on a few enthusiasts. 'Subject', 'prone' and 'liable' are all followed by 'to'.
explanation.cs: Za mezerou stojí 'on' a s ním se pojí jen 'reliant on' (závislý na). 'Subject', 'prone' i 'liable' chtějí 'to'.

explanation.en: 'Achieve results' is the natural collocation: 'have achieved remarkable results'. 'Won' goes with prizes or victories, and 'made results' is not English.
explanation.cs: Spojení 'achieve results' = dosáhnout výsledků. Česky 'udělat výsledky' svádí k 'made', ale anglicky to nejde; 'win' se pojí s cenou nebo vítězstvím.

explanation.en: 'At your own pace' is a fixed phrase meaning 'as fast or slowly as you want'. 'Stride' belongs to a different phrase, 'take something in your stride', which means to deal with it calmly.
explanation.cs: 'At one's own pace' = vlastním tempem. Česky 'tempo' láká k 'tempo', ale to se používá hlavně v hudbě; 'take sth in one's stride' je jiné spojení (zvládnout s klidem).

explanation.en: The gap is followed by a noun phrase ('these efforts') and a contrast is needed, so 'Despite' fits. 'Although' needs a full clause, and 'However' and 'Nevertheless' cannot take a noun phrase as their object.
explanation.cs: Za mezerou je jen podstatné jméno ('these efforts'), proto předložka 'Despite' (navzdory). 'Although' potřebuje celou větu s podmětem a slovesem.
